function: FL-trained DNN selects the transmit power region and beam-direction zone at cluster-head APs, jointly with multicast route-selection weights; RIS phases closed-form (pp. 4, 6, 12).
system: IoT MANET with cell-free massive MIMO: single-antenna UEs, single directional rotatable-antenna APs, reflecting RISs (default 60 RISs, 16 elements); 802.11a MAC, band unstated (pp. 3-4, 14).
method: Fully connected DNN (three hidden layers 128/64/64, ReLU) trained supervised on targets from a conventional optimizer, with federated averaging of CH models at the CPU (pp. 12-14).
data_channel: NS-3 3.35 simulation: log-distance path loss and Nakagami m=1 (Rayleigh) fading in YansWifiChannel; 184,000 simulated samples split 80:20 for training and testing (pp. 6, 14).
test_conditions: Training: simulated samples under unspecified diverse conditions, random 80:20 split. Testing: NS-3 runs over speeds 15-75 km/h, group sizes 5-20, 40-100 nodes, RPGM/RWP mobility (pp. 14-17).
baselines: MAODV, MAODV+CFLC, MAODV with conventional iteration-based clustering (non-learned routing); FLQMR, an earlier FL-based routing protocol of the authors [10]; FLEMR without clustering; local DNN without FL (pp. 14-15).
metrics: PDR, routing delay, control overhead, energy efficiency, spectral efficiency, cluster-head changes, prediction RMSE, cost-value convergence, average execution time (pp. 14-18).
complexity: Orders: FL training O(DEP+CP), route prediction O(UP), region-zone power allocation O(T(R+Z)); Table VI vs MAODV; execution time 0.335-0.679 s versus 4.12-22.78 s (pp. 13, 17-18).
openness: none (own NS-3 simulated data, no code or data link, p. 14)
q1_support: p. 14: "The log-distance propagation loss model is used to capture large-scale path loss, while the Nakagami model with m = 1 emulates Rayleigh fading" (custom NS-3 channel with textbook models; no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured data).
q2_support: p. 14: "randomly split into training and testing sets in an 80:20 ratio" (held-out part of the same simulated data; no test in a scenario or configuration excluded from training is stated).
q3_support: p. 14, Table VIII: "MAODV protocol without clustering [15]" and "The federated learning-enhanced QoS multicast routing (FLQMR) protocol without clustering [10]"; p. 15: "Scheme I consistently outperforms the other protocols" (PDR); p. 17: Scheme VI "results in lower EE".
q4_support: p. 13: "the complexity of adaptive transmit power allocation is O(T(R + Z))"; p. 17: "Scheme I consistently achieves significantly lower execution times, ranging from 0.335 to 0.679 s".
q5_support: p. 14: "These datasets were generated through simulations conducted under diverse network conditions" (own simulated data; no code or data link and no public channel dataset).
notes: Eligibility: most of the learning is above the PHY (route-selection weights; FL clustering from [13]), but the same FL-trained DNN (9 inputs; 6 outputs x1-x4, Region, Zone; p. 12 Fig. 11, p. 13 Table V) also decides the region (transmit power) and zone (beam direction) of each transmission, which the paper assigns to the physical layer (p. 4, Fig. 3: "Determines the optimal phase shift, region, beam zone, and transmit power"). It thus learns a PHY decision jointly with routing and passes check 4; area 3 through beams. Reviewer should confirm that a zone-based beam direction and power of a single directional AP antenna counts as beams rather than link adaptation (function). RIS phases are closed form (eq. 11, p. 6) and FL aggregation is digital FedAvg at the CPU over backhaul (p. 3; eq. 23, p. 13), so not area 7. q3: the learned baseline is FLQMR [10], an earlier FL routing protocol of the same authors with uniform power, compared on EE and SE (Fig. 16, p. 17); the local DNN of Fig. 13(b) is a variant and not counted. q1: NS-3 YansWifiChannel with log-distance and Nakagami m=1 is not a standardized model. Band not stated (802.11a MAC, Table VII, p. 14).
